limitations: A single serial owner is explicit. Concurrent independent NotificationService instances writing the same agent cache need a separate cross-process ownership model.

Hydration begins with a valid version-2 snapshot. Legacy migration, malformed coordinate rejection, group coalescing, expiry and notification category/priority policy remain separately test-covered and not modeled here.
Rows project title/body/data content to identity plus a read mark. Alias mutation of returned or input objects is outside this projection.
Storage operations are atomic but their outcome may be ambiguous to the caller. Restart in this case assumes a successful read of the durable version-2 snapshot.
Ordinary synchronous list/getUnreadCount APIs can observe provisional in-memory work. The DurableFence invariant concerns the quiescent native and durable-read APIs.
Conformance executes all 69 existing real SQLite/runtime tests. Named fault injection gates real API effects, and is not exhaustive schedule equivalence.
The finite capacity one represents the item/byte page boundary. Real tests check the actual encoded envelope and native byte limits without truncating records.
A sequence cursor can skip deleted/expired/superseded rows when no retained row exists at that sequence. The fence remains fixed across later appends.
Malformed arbitrary cursor numbers, unknown record fields and Unicode byte encoding are checked by existing implementation tests, outside the finite value domain.
Changing the inbox epoch invalidates old cursors. After that error the client must explicitly begin a new snapshot, which is outside this one-cursor model.
